issue.title: Deterministic parallel compilation for residuals/emissions and canonical certificate fragment assembly
issue.body:
This change addresses parallelization in the residual/emission/quantization/certification compilation layer while preserving canonical artifact determinism. The core requirement is that thread scheduling can change throughput, but must not change section bytes, offsets, or certificate CIDs.

- **Residual quantization + delta compilation (deterministic under parallelism)**
  - Added threaded APIs in `residual.rs`:
    - `quantize_logprobs_with_threads(...)`
    - `compute_residual_deltas_with_threads(...)`
  - Kept existing sequential APIs as wrappers (`...with_threads(..., 1)`).
  - Enforced canonical residual processing via stable key ordering and token dedup before delta computation, eliminating order-sensitive accumulation from input interleavings.

- **Emission packing with canonical parallel assembly**
  - Added `pack_emission_tables_with_threads(...)` in `pack.rs`.
  - Parallelized per-region fragment preparation, then performed deterministic merge by canonical region index.
  - Preserved dedup semantics and stable range assignment independent of worker completion order.

- **Certificate claim-fragment compilation with canonical CID materialization**
  - Added `Certificate::new_from_claim_fragments(...)` in `certificate.rs`.
  - Claim fragments can be assembled in parallel, then canonicalized via sort + dedup before CID computation.
  - Ensures certificate payload bytes and resulting CIDs remain invariant across thread counts/interleavings.

- **Determinism-focused coverage additions**
  - Added focused tests for:
    - quantization thread-count invariance
    - residual-delta canonical/thread-invariant output
    - emission packing thread-count invariance
    - canonical claim-fragment assembly yielding identical certificate bytes/CIDs

```rust
let cert = Certificate::new_from_claim_fragments(
    source_cid,
    corpus_cid,
    graph_cid,
    metric_cid,
    op_cid,
    benchmark_cid,
    &claim_fragments,
    attestation,
    threads, // 1, 2, 4, ...
)?;
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #173

reviews.body:
## Pull request overview This PR introduces thread-bounded, deterministic-by-construction parallelism in the graph compilation layer (residual quantization/deltas, emission packing) and in certificate claim-fragment assembly, with tests intended to ensure byte/CID invariance across thread counts. **Changes:** - Add `*_with_threads(...)` APIs for quantization, residual delta computation, and emission packing, keeping sequential wrappers. - Canonicalize residual delta computation inputs (sort + dedup) and emission packing assembly order (sort fragments by region index) to preserve deterministic outputs under parallel execution. - Add determinism-focused unit tests covering thread-count invariance for quantization, residual deltas, emission packing, and certificate claim-fragment assembly. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 4 out of 4 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | crates/uor-r4-graph-compiler/src/residual.rs | Adds threaded quantization + residual-delta APIs and determinism tests; introduces canonicalization + executor-based mapping. | | crates/uor-r4-graph-compiler/src/pack.rs | Adds threaded emission packing with deterministic fragment merge and a thread-invariance test. | | crates/uor-r4-graph-certify/src/certificate.rs | Adds canonical claim-fragment constructor with parallel cloning + canonical sort/dedup prior to CID materialization. | | crates/uor-r4-graph-certify/tests/certificate_test.rs | Adds a test asserting canonical/thread-invariant claim-fragment assembly yields identical certificates. |
Comments suppressed due to low confidence (1) **crates/uor-r4-graph-certify/src/certificate.rs:164** * `canonical_sort_and_dedup_claims` currently uses `sort_by_key(Self::claim_key)` where `claim_key` allocates by cloning `name` and `slice_label` for every comparison/key extraction (and twice again during `dedup_by_key`). This can become a significant allocation hot spot when assembling many claim fragments; it’s avoidable by sorting/deduping via comparisons on borrowed fields. ``` fn canonical_sort_and_dedup_claims(claims: &mut Vec) { claims.sort_by_key(Self::claim_key); claims.dedup_by_key(|c| Self::claim_key(c)); } ```

review_comments.body: `quantize_logprobs` now panics on mismatched `tokens`/`logprobs` lengths via `expect(...)`. Previously it used `zip` and would deterministically truncate to the shorter slice; introducing a panic here makes this public API less robust for recoverable input errors.

`map_with_threads` treats `threads == 0` as sequential because of the `threads <= 1` check. This prevents using the executor’s documented `RayonExecutor::new(0)` behavior (auto = `available_parallelism()`), and makes `threads=0` inconsistent across call sites.

`map_with_threads` treats `threads == 0` as sequential because of the `threads <= 1` check. This blocks the executor’s `RayonExecutor::new(0)` auto-thread behavior and makes `threads=0` unusable for “use all cores”.

`claims_from_fragments_with_threads` treats `threads == 0` as sequential due to `threads <= 1`. This prevents using the executor’s `RayonExecutor::new(0)` auto-thread behavior (available_parallelism), which is likely what callers expect when passing 0.

This issue also appears on line 161 of the same file.
